title: When the Ground Turns Dangerous
question: How do people reduce the harm that geologic hazards cause?
hook: An avalanche falling into a mountain lake can start a debris flow whose effects reach hundreds of miles away.
idea: Geologic hazards can be avoided, engineered against, planned around and watched from above, and even giant eruptions can reach Earth's climate.

beats.prompt: High in the mountains, an avalanche slams into a lake. What can happen next?

choices.label: The lake simply absorbs the snow
choices.feedback: It is tempting to think a lake soaks up the blow, but the impact can trigger a chain of events.

choices.label: A debris flow with effects far downstream
Only a small local wave forms
choices.feedback: The effects are not necessarily local: they can reach far beyond the lake.

beats.explain: In mountain regions, an avalanche hitting a lake can cause a debris flow, with consequences potentially hundreds of miles away.

beats.prompt: Match each problem to a method used against it.
beats.explain: Each kind of hazard has its own tools, from walls that hold slopes to maps that steer building toward safer ground.

beats.prompt: Planners want precise, up-to-date views of where land is shifting across a whole region. Which tool fits best?

choices.label: Old paper maps from a century ago
choices.feedback: Old maps cannot show what the ground is doing now.

choices.label: Asking residents what they remember
choices.feedback: Memories help, but they are neither precise nor timely across a whole region.

beats.explain: Earth Observation, often backed by ground surveys, lets people map and monitor geohazards with precision and timeliness.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: Eleven flood basalt episodes occurred in the past 250 million years.
Six of the eleven known provinces line up with periods of global warming.
So every large volcanic province caused global warming.
The overlap suggests volcanic CO₂ can affect the climate.
beats.explain: Only six of the eleven line up with warming, so the evidence cannot show that every province caused it.
